answer: Model the attacker's bill, not the honest user's. Fabricating one identity costs a keypair, one proof-of-work stamp, and three independent attestations, each expiring after two epochs unless renewed by fresh work. Renewal means a new signed task, so the farm pays again every twelve hours. A garden of a thousand puppets carries a recurring cost that grows with each re-attestation. What breaks first is the budget, not the cryptography. A plume of fake history cannot outlive two epochs, and the echo of an expired vouch is silence.
